title: NASA Announces $20 Billion "Ignition" Plan for a Permanent Moon Base
summary:
NASA now wants to move beyond short Moon visits and build a place where people can stay.

On March 24, 2026, NASA unveiled a $20 billion initiative called "Ignition." Its aim is to build a permanent base on the Moon and test whether humans can sustainably live beyond Earth. The plan marks a major shift from short lunar visits to a long-term human presence.

The base is planned for the area near the lunar south pole. NASA chose the region because scientists believe water ice is trapped inside some of its permanently shadowed craters. The area also has places that receive sunlight for long periods, which could help provide power for a future base.

The plan has three phases. From 2026 through 2029, robotic missions will head to the lunar south pole. These uncrewed flights will deliver rovers and scientific instruments, explore the area and help scientists identify good locations for the base. The missions will also test new systems and help NASA learn how to operate on the Moon.

From 2029 through 2032, NASA will begin building infrastructure for longer missions, including early power systems, cargo and communications systems, and initial living spaces. International partners will play a major role in this phase. Japan's space agency, JAXA, is developing a pressurized rover that will let astronauts live and work inside it while traveling long distances across the lunar surface.

The third and final phase begins in 2032 and focuses on establishing a permanent lunar outpost where astronauts can live and work for extended periods. NASA plans to add larger habitats, communications equipment and transportation systems. A nuclear power plant is also planned to provide steady energy during the long lunar nights.

"The moon base will help NASA learn how to live away from Earth, and possibly later to Mars and other planets," said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman.
why_it_matters: The plan marks a shift from short visits to a long-term human presence on the Moon. NASA says it will help the agency learn how to live away from Earth.
